references.text: Sarai gives Hagar to Abram as a wife – the background to the family conflict that eventually leads to Hagar being sent away.
Abram leaves Hagar in Sarai's hands, and Hagar flees into the wilderness – a precursor to the final expulsion.
Sarah demands that Abraham send away the slave woman and her son, which directly triggers Abraham's action.
God assures Abraham that Ishmael will also become a nation, giving Abraham courage to obey Sarah's demand.
Abraham rises early in the morning to sacrifice Isaac – the same phrasing (וַיַּשְׁכֵּם אַבְרָהָם בַּבֹּקֶר) shows Abraham's obedience in painful situations.
Hagar wanders in the wilderness until the water runs out, but God hears the boy's cry and shows her a well – the direct continuation of the expulsion.
Ishmael's descendants and his twelve princes fulfill God's promise that Ishmael would become a great nation.
Paul interprets the story of Hagar and Sarah allegorically: the slave woman and her son were sent away, for the slave woman's son shall not inherit with the free woman's son.
